articles.title: Pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary vascular disease, and right ventricular adaptation in transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) commonly coexists with pulmonary hypertension (PH), which is associated with adverse outcomes after transcatheter tricuspid valve intervention (TTVI). However, the prognostic impact of PH subtypes and pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) thresholds in this setting remains insufficiently defined. We evaluated guideline-based PH classifications and their association with outcomes in a large real-world TTVI cohort.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In an international multicenter registry, 903 patients with severe TR undergoing TTVI underwent pre-procedural right heart catheterization and were followed for up to two years. PH was defined as mean pulmonary artery pressure >20 mmHg, and PVR was stratified according to guideline thresholds. Endpoints included procedural success, New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class, and all-cause mortality.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: PH was present in 88% of patients; among patients with PH, median PVR was 2.7 WU. A pre-capillary component (PVR >2 WU) was observed in 68%, including 13% with PVR >5 WU. Procedural success was 81%. NYHA functional class improved significantly from baseline to follow-up irrespective of PH status or PVR. Mortality increased with PH and higher PVR. A PVR threshold of >2 WU alone did not discriminate survival, whereas PVR >5 WU identified a high-risk phenotype. An integrated classification combining PH status, PVR >5 WU, and RV-PA uncoupling (TAPSE/PASP <0.30 mm/mmHg) provided effective prognostic stratification.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: High procedural success and symptomatic improvement were observed following TTVI across PH subgroups. Although infrequent among TTVI patients, a PVR >5 WU identifies a high-risk phenotype with increased mortality. Comprehensive hemodynamic profiling improves risk stratification and may support patient counselling and informed decision-making.

articles.conclusion: High procedural success and symptomatic improvement were observed following TTVI across PH subgroups. Although infrequent among TTVI patients, a PVR >5 WU identifies a high-risk phenotype with increased mortality. Comprehensive hemodynamic profiling improves risk stratification and may support patient counselling and informed decision-making.

articles.title: Artesunate Ameliorates Hypoxia-Induced Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in Rats

abstract.text: Artesunate (Art) is a semi-synthetic derivative of artemisinin derived from traditional Chinese medicine, characterized by a unique endoperoxide bridge structure and exhibiting broad pharmacological activities with diverse mechanisms. In recent years, studies have demonstrated its beneficial effects in anti-inflammation, anti-oxidative stress, anti-fibrosis, and anti-tumorigenesis. However, the effects of artesunate on hypoxic pulmonary hypertension (HPH) and its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the therapeutic effects of artesunate in a rat model of HPH and its possible mechanisms of action. Six-to eight-week-old SD rats were randomly assigned to five groups: a control group, a 28-day hypoxia model group, and three groups exposed to 28 days of hypoxia and treated with low, medium, or high doses of artesunate, respectively. Pulmonary artery pressure was assessed by echocardiography and right heart catheterization. Immunohistochemistry and Western blotting were used to detect the protein expression levels of M1/M2 macrophage markers, p-AMPK, and ACE2 in lung tissues. Compared with the model group, artesunate-treated groups exhibited a significant dose-dependent improvement in pulmonary hypertension. The model group demonstrated increased M1 macrophage infiltration and reduced expression of p-AMPK and ACE2 in lung tissues. Artesunate attenuates hypoxic pulmonary hypertension in rats, which may be associated with reduced M1 macrophage infiltration and restored expression of p-AMPK and ACE2.

articles.title: DHEA-S in Pulmonary Hypertension: Insights from PVDOMICS

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) associates with disease severity in pulmonary hypertension (PH). However, prior studies focused on Group 1 disease; it is unknown whether DHEA-S associates with PH severity in other etiologies. It also remains unclear if DHEA-S associations with PH severity differ by sex or menopausal status.

abstract.label: RESEARCH QUESTION
abstract.text: Do associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity differ by PH etiology, sex, or menopausal status?

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: We analyzed data from PVDOMICS, including 85 healthy controls and 710 participants with PH. Venous plasma DHEA-S levels were measured by ultraperformance liquid chromatography mass spectrometry. Multivariable regression models were used to examine associations between DHEA-S levels and invasive hemodynamics, right ventricular (RV) systolic function, and six-minute walk distance (6MWD). Analyses were stratified by sex and WSPH group, with exploratory stratification by menopausal status among subjects with Group 1 PH.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: DHEA-S levels were lower in all WSPH Groups compared with controls (adjusted p<0.01 for all). Associations between DHEA-S levels and PH severity metrics appeared most prominent in females with Group 1 PH. A doubling of DHEA-S was associated with a 2.8 mmHg (95% CI 1.6-4.1) lower mean pulmonary artery pressure, 3.2% (95% CI 2.0-4.4%) higher RV ejection fraction, and 22m (95% CI 11-33) farther 6MWD (all p<0.01). Higher DHEA-S associated with better RV function, but not pulmonary hemodynamics or 6MWD in females with Group 2 PH and males with Group 3 PH. In Group 1 PH, associations between DHEA-S and measures of PH severity appeared stronger in post-menopausal compared with premenopausal females.

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: Lower DHEA-S is a consistent feature across PH etiologies, but its association with disease severity appeared most pronounced in females with Group 1 PH. Modulation of DHEA-S levels or the pathways governing its regulation may represent a therapeutic target in PH, warranting further mechanistic study.

articles.conclusion: Lower DHEA-S is a consistent feature across PH etiologies, but its association with disease severity appeared most pronounced in females with Group 1 PH. Modulation of DHEA-S levels or the pathways governing its regulation may represent a therapeutic target in PH, warranting further mechanistic study.

articles.title: Ruptured Tricuspid Hydatid Cyst Causing Nonthrombotic Pulmonary Embolism and Right Ventricular Failure Requiring VA-ECMO

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiac echinococcosis is rare, and tricuspid valve involvement is exceptionally uncommon. Ruptured right-sided cysts can mimic acute pulmonary embolism, delaying diagnosis.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 20-year-old Yemeni man presented with acute dyspnea, fever, and collapse. Imaging demonstrated bilateral pulmonary artery filling defects with right ventricular strain and a large mobile tricuspid valve mass. Refractory hypoxemia and obstructive shock developed despite maximal medical therapy, prompting venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation. Transesophageal echocardiography identified a heterogeneous cystic lesion and a patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunting. Emergent surgery revealed a ruptured tricuspid leaflet hydatid cyst; histopathology and serology confirmed Echinococcus.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Not all pulmonary artery filling defects are thrombotic. This case demonstrates nonthrombotic pulmonary embolism from ruptured cardiac hydatid cyst and the role of venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation as a bridge to diagnosis and surgical management in acute right ventricular failure from obstructive intracardiac pathology.

articles.title: Staged Tricuspid Valve-in-Valve Replacement in Atrial Switch With Ventricular Dysfunction, Limited Vascular Access, and Tachyarrhythmia

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients with dextro-transposition of the great arteries and atrial switch frequently experience baffle stenosis/leak, arrhythmias, systemic ventricular dysfunction, and tricuspid dysfunction.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 40-year-old man with dextro-transposition of the great arteries and atrial switch underwent surgical tricuspid valve replacement at age 24. He presented with worsening exertional dyspnea, narrow complex tachycardia, ventricular dysfunction, and severe tricuspid valve regurgitation/stenosis. The patient had atresia of the left femoral vein and superior vena cava baffle, with severe right common iliac vein stenosis. He underwent staged procedures including right iliac vein angioplasty, ablation, and transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement via superior vena cava baffle puncture.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case highlights the feasibility of transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement through careful procedural planning and staged management.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Transcatheter interventions are feasible in high-risk patients with congenital anatomy, limited vascular access, poor hemodynamic reserve, and high reoperation risk, with a staged systematic approach to minimize risk and advanced planning for emergency mechanical circulatory support.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Pulsus Alternans: A Hemodynamic Harbinger of Right Heart Failure
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstract.text: Right ventricular (RV) pulsus alternans is a rare hemodynamic finding in patients with advanced heart failure. While pulsus alternans is classically associated with left ventricular failure, its appearance in the right ventricle carries distinct prognostic and management implications. We present the case of a 66-year-old patient with end-stage heart failure who exhibited RV pulsus alternans during right heart catheterization. This finding served as a harbinger of clinical deterioration and suggested a poor prognosis for isolated left ventricular mechanical circulatory support. Recognition of this sign is vital for clinicians to guide appropriate decision-making regarding advanced mechanical circulatory support and transplantation.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Rescue Management of Life-Threatening Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Using Off-Label Sotatercept for Pre-Delivery Hemodynamic Optimization: A Case Report

abstract.text: Pregnancy in women with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) carries substantial maternal and fetal risks, particularly with severe or poorly controlled disease. This case report describes a 24-year-old woman with severe PAH (mean pulmonary arterial pressure [mPAP], 71 mmHg) diagnosed at 22 weeks of gestation after presenting with hemoptysis. Despite combination therapy with macitentan, sildenafil, intravenous epoprostenol, and inhaled treprostinil, pulmonary arterial pressure remained markedly elevated, and epoprostenol up-titration was limited by thrombocytopenia (platelet count, 79 × 109/L). As continued pregnancy posed an imminent threat to maternal life, early delivery was planned; however, the perioperative hemodynamic risk remained extremely high. Subcutaneous sotatercept (0.3 mg/kg) was administered off-label at 23 weeks and 6 days of gestation to optimize hemodynamics before delivery. One day later, mPAP decreased from 71 to 60 mmHg, whereas pulmonary vascular resistance decreased from 17.7 to 9.14 Wood units. Cesarean delivery under general anesthesia was performed at 24 weeks and 1 day of gestation with therapeutic phlebotomy and reinfusion, invasive hemodynamic monitoring, vasoactive support, inhaled nitric oxide, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation standby. Both the mother and infant survived. Maternal genetic testing identified a pathogenic BMPR2 variant. Recent case reports suggest that sotatercept may rapidly improve hemodynamics in PAH. However, as multiple therapies were administered concurrently, its contribution to the observed improvement could not be determined, and its safety during pregnancy remains unknown. This case report highlights the potential role of individualized pre-delivery hemodynamic optimization in multidisciplinary management of exceptionally severe PAH during pregnancy.

articles.title: Pulmonary Hypertension as a Risk Factor for Stroke: Veteran Affairs Right Heart Catheterization Cohort Study

abstract.text: The contribution of pulmonary hypertension (PH) to stroke risk remains incompletely understood, particularly across hemodynamic subgroups. We aimed to evaluate the association between hemodynamically confirmed PH and incident stroke, with emphasis on PH subgroups. In this retrospective cohort study, patients undergoing right heart catheterization were included and classified as precapillary, postcapillary, combined, and other based on right heart catheterization findings. The main outcome was the incidence of stroke. Multivariable Cox proportional hazard models were also used to assess the relationship between PH and stroke. Among 7106 patients, 75.5% had PH (24.2% precapillary, 29.4% isolated postcapillary, 33.8% combined, and 12.5% other). Over 22,528 person-years of follow-up, stroke incidence was higher in patients with PH compared with those without PH (3.98 vs. 2.51 per 100 person-years, p < 0.001). Stroke incidence was highest in combined PH (5.13 per 100 person-years), followed by postcapillary (4.27) and precapillary PH (3.41; p < 0.01 across groups). In the multivariable model, PH and its subgroups were not independently associated with stroke after adjustment for demographic and cardiovascular covariates. In conclusion, PH is not an independent determinant of stroke; however, patients with PH have a significantly higher stroke incidence, particularly those with postcapillary PH. Therefore, patients with PH represent a clinically vulnerable group in whom careful assessment of traditional risk factors and use of aggressive primary prevention for stroke may be important.

articles.title: Wearable Tissue Oximetry in Cardiogenic Shock: Microcirculatory Deterioration Preceding Macrohemodynamic Collapse

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiogenic shock can progress rapidly, even when conventional macrohemodynamic vital signs remain stable. Continuous, noninvasive microcirculatory monitoring is uncommon but could provide early signals of impending decompensation.

abstract.label: FIH/EARLY REPORTS SUMMARY
abstract.text: The authors report near-infrared spectroscopy and photoplethysmography monitoring with the investigational NIRSense Envello Core wearable device. The patient was a 66-year-old man with complex valvular disease and combined pre/post capillary pulmonary hypertension, who rapidly deteriorated and died despite intensive care unit management.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Chest-derived tissue oxygen saturation and perfusion index appeared to signal deterioration ∼4 hours before clinically recognized collapse, and correlated strongly with central venous pressure (r = -0.95; perfusion index) and systolic pulmonary artery pressure (r = 0.87; tissue oxygen saturation).

abstract.label: NOVELTY
abstract.text: To our knowledge, this is the first continuous microcirculatory characterization of the transition to terminal cardiogenic shock using a wearable near-infrared spectroscopy and photoplethysmography device.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Noninvasive microcirculatory monitoring may detect hemodynamic collapse before conventional vital signs, identifying a potential window for earlier intervention.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Reverse Remodeling Without Pulmonary Vascular Unloading During Sotatercept Therapy: An Invasive Pressure-Volume Loop Study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Sotatercept improves hemodynamics and functional capacity in pulmonary arterial hypertension; however, its direct actions on the right ventricle (RV) remain poorly understood. We investigated whether sotatercept exerts intrinsic RV protective effects beyond pulmonary vascular unloading.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: In this registry-based cohort study, 28 consecutive patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension between April 2024 and September 2025 underwent right-heart catheterization with conductance-catheter RV pressure-volume analysis and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging before sotatercept initiation and again after a median of 6.1 months of treatment. Hemodynamic nonresponse was defined as a decrease in mean pulmonary arterial pressure by <10%. Reproducibility was tested in 2 independent sotatercept-treated cohorts (SPECTRA [Sotatercept Phase 2 Exploratory Clinical Trial in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension], n=20, cardiac magnetic resonance; Cologne, n=20, echocardiography).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 28 patients (17 [61%] female; median age, 48 [IQR, 34-67] years), 21 (75%) were responders and 7 (25%) nonresponders. In responders, sotatercept significantly decreased mean pulmonary arterial pressure (52.0 [IQR, 49.0-65.0] to 39.0 [IQR, 32.0-42.0] mm Hg; P<0.001) and pulmonary vascular resistance (10.7±3.9 to 6.7±2.3 Wood units; P<0.001) without changing cardiac output, reduced RV end-diastolic volume (222 [IQR, 183-242] to 160 [IQR, 129-204] mL; P<0.001) and RV mass (42.8 [IQR, 33.6-56.0] to 33.1 [IQR, 28.2-44.4] g; P<0.001), and improved 6-minute walk distance by +64 m (95% CI, 27 to 102; P=0.002). Ventricular-arterial coupling (end-systolic/arterial elastance) improved although load-independent contractility decreased alongside the decrease in effective arterial elastance. By contrast, nonresponders demonstrated a clinical-hemodynamic disconnect. Despite persistently elevated RV afterload and unchanged end-systolic/arterial elastance, a significant reduction in RV mass (56.1 [IQR, 45.9-81.0] to 46.4 [IQR, 35.9-59.4] g; P=0.003) was observed, accompanied by a significant decrease in B-type natriuretic peptide levels, whereas 6-minute walk distance did not change significantly (+15 m [95% CI, -12 to 42]; P=0.23); the difference in 6-minute walk distance change between groups did not reach significance (P=0.10). Reduction in RV mass and chamber size was observed in the absence of pulmonary vascular unloading among hemodynamic nonresponders to sotatercept in 2 independent cohorts.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In primary and validation cohorts, structural RV reverse remodeling after sotatercept initiation occurred independent of pulmonary vascular unloading. This pattern is not fully explained by pulmonary vascular unloading and raises the possibility of an effect of sotatercept on the myocardium itself. Improvement in exercise capacity was observed within the hemodynamic responder group only.

articles.conclusion: In primary and validation cohorts, structural RV reverse remodeling after sotatercept initiation occurred independent of pulmonary vascular unloading. This pattern is not fully explained by pulmonary vascular unloading and raises the possibility of an effect of sotatercept on the myocardium itself. Improvement in exercise capacity was observed within the hemodynamic responder group only.

articles.title: Cardiac and Metabolic Effects of Semaglutide in Obesity-Related HFpEF: Rationale and Design of CAMEO-SEMA

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Two-thirds of patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) have obesity, and >90% have increased visceral adiposity. Adiposity-associated HFpEF is characterized by hemodynamic congestion driven by impaired cardiac reserve, volume overload and altered blood distribution, adverse cardiac remodeling, pericardial constraint, systemic vascular stiffening, myosteatosis, metabolic dysfunction, and altered adipokine signaling profiles. Recent clinical trials have demonstrated that glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists alleviate symptoms and improve exercise capacity in patients with obesity-related HFpEF, but the mechanisms underlying these benefits remain uncertain.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aims to elucidate the mechanisms by which semaglutide improves clinical status in patients with HFpEF and obesity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The CAMEO-SEMA trial is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled mechanistic trial evaluating the effects of semaglutide in obesity-related HFpEF.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eighty-one participants have been randomized in a 2:1 ratio to semaglutide subcutaneously once weekly or matching placebo for 52 weeks. Comprehensive pathophysiological characterization is being performed at baseline and following treatment, including invasive exercise hemodynamic status, transcardiac (arterial and coronary sinus) blood sampling at rest and with exercise, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, submaximal and peak aerobic capacity through expired gas analysis, comprehensive rest and exercise echocardiography, body composition and visceral adiposity assessment, blood volume analysis, oral glucose testing, subcutaneous adipose tissue biopsy, and inflammatory-adipokine profiling.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: The CAMEO-SEMA trial will provide comprehensive, novel insights into the mechanisms by which the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists semaglutide affects the key pathophysiological factors causing symptoms, exercise limitation, and morbidity in patients with obesity-related HFpEF. (Cardiac and Metabolic Effects of Semaglutide [CAMEO-SEMA]; NCT05371496).

articles.conclusion: The CAMEO-SEMA trial will provide comprehensive, novel insights into the mechanisms by which the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists semaglutide affects the key pathophysiological factors causing symptoms, exercise limitation, and morbidity in patients with obesity-related HFpEF. (Cardiac and Metabolic Effects of Semaglutide [CAMEO-SEMA]; NCT05371496).

articles.title: Defining the Right Ventricular Burden in HFpEF: What Seals the Fate of the Right Ventricle?
articles.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology

articles.title: Sildenafil for Fetal Growth Restriction - An Individual Participant Meta-Analysis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors have been investigated as an in utero therapy for fetal growth restriction (FGR).

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis of randomized trials of phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitors versus placebo/no treatment in singleton pregnancies with FGR. The primary outcome was infant survival without serious adverse outcome. Secondary outcomes included gestation at birth and birth weight z score among liveborn infants. Predefined subgroups were evaluated.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 19 eligible trials, 4 contributed data. Of 492 participants, 240 had been assigned to placebo and 252 to the phosphodiesterase type-5 inhibitor sildenafil. Infant survival without serious adverse outcome occurred in 110 of 240 participants (45.8%) assigned to placebo versus 113 of 252 participants (44.8%) assigned to sildenafil (relative risk [RR], 0.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78 to 1.17). No apparent interaction was observed between subgroups. There was no apparent difference in gestation at birth (mean difference -0.5 weeks; 95% CI, -1.3 to 0.2) or birth weight z score (mean difference, 0.0; 95% CI, -0.2 to 0.2). Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn occurred in 10 of 176 participants (5.7%) assigned to placebo versus 27 of 197 participants (13.7%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 2.39; 95% CI, 1.23 to 4.61); nitric oxide was used in 15 of 176 participants (8.5%) assigned to placebo versus 20 of 197 participants (10.2%) assigned to sildenafil (RR, 1.21; 95% CI, 0.64 to 2.29).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Maternal sildenafil therapy for FGR was not associated with improved outcomes for infants. It was associated with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn but not with an increase in nitric oxide therapy. (Funded by Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; PROSPERO number, CRD42017069688; ANZCTR number, ACTRN12612000584831; ISRCTN number, ISRCTN39133303; ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT02442492 and NCT02277132.).

articles.conclusion: Maternal sildenafil therapy for FGR was not associated with improved outcomes for infants. It was associated with persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn but not with an increase in nitric oxide therapy. (Funded by Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; PROSPERO number, CRD42017069688; ANZCTR number, ACTRN12612000584831; ISRCTN number, ISRCTN39133303; ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT02442492 and NCT02277132.).

articles.title: Transcatheter Valve Repair of Tricuspid Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the TriCLASP Study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair is a viable option for patients with ≥severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR).

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study aims to evaluate 2-year outcomes with the PASCAL transcatheter valve repair system from the TriCLASP European, single-arm, postmarket clinical follow-up study, including outcomes stratified by baseline TR severity.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: The TriCLASP study evaluated the safety and effectiveness of tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair with the PASCAL system. TR reduction and clinical, functional, and quality of life outcomes were assessed at 2 years. Outcomes were also assessed by baseline TR severity (≤moderate vs ≥severe TR).

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: In 300 enrolled patients, mean age was 80.1 years, 52.0% were women, and 75.8% had ≥severe TR. Significant and sustained TR reduction was observed from baseline to 2 years, with ≤moderate TR achieved in 81.3% (P < 0.001). The 2-year Kaplan-Meier estimates for survival and freedom from heart failure hospitalization (HFH) were 77.5% ± 2.6% and 71.9% ± 2.8%, respectively, with a 71.4% decrease in annualized HFH rate (P < 0.001). Patients experienced significant improvements in functional capacity and quality of life at 2 years (NYHA functional class I/II: 73.2%; 6-minute walk distance: +26.6 m; Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score: +7.3 points; all P < 0.001). Outcomes were similar in patients stratified by baseline ≤moderate and ≥severe TR, including significant TR reduction and meaningful clinical, functional, and quality-of-life improvements.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Outcomes from the TriCLASP study confirm durable safety and effectiveness of the PASCAL system at 2 years in a postmarket setting. Results demonstrated significant and sustained TR reduction, favorable survival, reduced HFH, and clinically meaningful improvements in symptoms, function, and quality of life, which were consistent across patients with moderate and severe TR.

articles.conclusion: Outcomes from the TriCLASP study confirm durable safety and effectiveness of the PASCAL system at 2 years in a postmarket setting. Results demonstrated significant and sustained TR reduction, favorable survival, reduced HFH, and clinically meaningful improvements in symptoms, function, and quality of life, which were consistent across patients with moderate and severe TR.

articles.title: Innovations in Temporary Mechanical Circulatory Support in Cardiogenic Shock
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.text: Temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) can provide rapid hemodynamic stabilization in cardiogenic shock (CS), creating a bridge to myocardial recovery, durable MCS or heart transplantation. Contemporary platforms remain constrained by risk of vascular and hemocompatability-related adverse events, restricted patient mobility and support duration. These limitations have become increasingly relevant as tMCS use expands beyond acute myocardial infarction-related CS to the highly heterogeneous heart failure-related and postcardiotomy shock states. Next generation tMCS technologies seek to address these issues through lower-profile access, improved hemocompatibility, dedicated right- and biventricular support, extended support duration with greater support capabilities, enhanced patient mobility, and integrated physiologic monitoring. This State-of-the-Art Review examines the design rationale, technological maturity, and emerging clinical evidence for these platforms, while highlighting clinical, data-related, engineering and regulatory gaps in the field. Ultimately, the challenge for next-generation tMCS is not simply to deliver greater flow, but to provide appropriate, phenotype-directed circulatory support while minimizing the biological, vascular, and operational costs.

articles.title: Young adulthood after thoracic organ transplantation: Developmental vulnerability, risk, and protection in recipients aged 18-24 years

abstract.text: Thoracic organ transplant recipients aged 18-24 years represent a distinct high-risk group with discordant early and longer-term outcomes. After heart transplantation, early survival is relatively favorable, yet 5-year survival conditional on 1-year survival is lowest in this age group among adult recipients and appears descriptively lower than the pediatric age-group estimates. This vulnerability is often attributed to medication nonadherence and care-transition challenges. Although these factors remain important and modifiable, they may not fully explain the excess risk during late adolescence and emerging adulthood. We propose that the 18-24 year period may be a developmental vulnerability window in which neurocognitive and psychological maturation intersects with pharmacokinetic variability, cardiometabolic changes, and transplant-specific stressors. Ongoing maturation of executive function, emotional regulation, identity formation, and self-management capacity may contribute to variable immunosuppressant exposure, missed surveillance, mental-health burden, and disruptions in care continuity. Recognizing this developmental context may improve risk stratification and inform integrated monitoring strategies that combine adherence support with medication-exposure assessment, psychological care, and structured transition. Age-stratified studies are needed to identify the factors that contribute to poor outcomes in this population and determine whether developmentally tailored care improves long-term survival.

articles.title: Impact of Cannulation on Venous Congestion, Right Ventricular Function, and End-Organ Protection During VV ECMO: A Computational Study
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Cannulation strategy during veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO) may influence venous drainage, right ventricular loading, and end-organ perfusion beyond gas exchange. We compared four cannulation strategies using a computational hemodynamic framework: pulmonary dual-lumen, Avalon dual-lumen, femoro-jugular, and femoro-femoral VV-ECMO, with three cannula sizes/configurations for each strategy and 10 virtual adult patients per configuration (120 simulations). Cannulation strategy was strongly associated with residual venous congestion and simulated organ dysfunction. Pulmonary dual-lumen support showed the most favorable size-dependent profile. The 31 Fr configuration achieved the lowest central venous pressure (8.8 ± 1.2 mm Hg), smallest inferior vena cava diameter (17.6 ± 1.6 mm), and greatest improvement in tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion (+5.4 ± 1.0 mm). It was also associated with the lowest creatinine, bilirubin, simulated dialysis risk, and hepatic dysfunction. Femoro-femoral VV-ECMO showed the least favorable profile despite preserved flow capability. These findings suggest that cannulation geometry may be an important determinant of venous decongestion, right-heart interaction, and simulated cardio-renal-hepatic protection beyond extracorporeal flow alone.

articles.title: Forging the Interventional Heart Failure Specialist: A JACC: Advances Expert Panel

abstract.text: Interventional heart failure (IHF) integrates advanced heart failure management with catheter-based procedural expertise to address clinical scenarios that neither interventional cardiology nor advanced heart failure and transplant cardiology can optimally manage alone. Despite growing clinical need, no standardized training pathway, competency framework, or workforce infrastructure exists. This Expert Panel proposes a comprehensive framework comprising: a core-and-track taxonomy defining 5 universal competency clusters and 5 procedural track domains; 13 clinical activities structured using entrustable professional activity methodology as pathway-agnostic training endpoints; multiple training pathways evaluated against shared competency benchmarks; and implementation guidance including a three-phase pilot-to-accreditation strategy, consortium models, hybrid compensation structures, and a minimum viable registry to generate comparative effectiveness evidence. Realization requires multisociety consensus, pilot program data, and collective commitment to building the training and evidence infrastructure needed to advance interventional heart failure toward recognized subspecialty status.

articles.title: Time-Evolving In Situ Coronary Thrombosis During Durable LVAD Support

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Myocardial infarction during durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support is usually attributed to pump thromboembolism or anticoagulation failure; in situ coronary thrombosis arising from local vascular pathology is rarely recognized.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A patient with pre-implant angiography confirming patent coronary arteries developed acute left anterior descending artery occlusion during long-term continuous-flow LVAD support. Intravascular ultrasound showed mural-adherent thrombus at the coronary bifurcation with negative remodeling and intact distal architecture, distinguishing in situ thrombosis from embolic occlusion. Aspiration thrombectomy without stenting restored normal flow.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Nonpulsatile hemodynamics, endothelial dysfunction, and recurrent bacteremia likely converged to produce coronary thrombosis independent of conventional embolic mechanisms, a scenario infrequently described in the LVAD literature and relevant to clinicians evaluating unexplained myocardial infarction in this population.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: In situ coronary thrombosis is an underrecognized, mechanistically distinct cause of myocardial infarction during LVAD support. Serial coronary imaging with intravascular ultrasound aids diagnosis and can guide thrombus-directed therapy without unnecessary stenting.

articles.title: Diastolic dysfunction in adults with congenital heart disease

abstract.text: Diastolic dysfunction is a major determinant of cardiovascular symptoms, quality of life, and overall prognosis in adults with acquired heart disease. The global burden of disease is increasing, and substantial progress has been made in developing standardized multimodality approaches for the assessment of left ventricular diastolic function. In adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) diastolic dysfunction is substantially more prevalent than in the general population; however, it remains comparatively under-investigated, under-diagnosed, and under-treated. Assessment is complicated by the marked heterogeneity of this population, including the influence of underlying anatomy, prior surgical interventions, and residual haemodynamic lesions on ventricular filling physiology. Consequently, a 'one-size-fits-all' approach or direct extrapolation of guidelines from acquired heart disease is often inappropriate. This state-of-the-art review summarized the current evidence and contemporary approaches to the assessment and management of diastolic dysfunction in ACHD, highlighting the strengths and limitations of available diagnostic modalities. In addition, lesion-specific considerations and practical diagnostic and management frameworks are proposed to evaluate and treat diastolic dysfunction across the spectrum of ACHD.

articles.title: Right Ventricular Outflow Tract Stenting in a 1.5 kg Premature Infant With Tetralogy of Fallot

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: This study describes successful transcatheter right ventricular outflow tract (RVOT) stenting in a premature infant with tetralogy of Fallot weighing 1.5 kg as a bridge to definitive repair.

abstract.label: KEY STEPS
abstract.text: Femoral venous access was obtained using a 4-F long sheath. Access to the RVOT was obtained using a 0.035-inch Wholey wire; the sheath provided a method for sighting angiography with protection of the tricuspid valve for stent delivery. Two overlapping drug-eluting stents were deployed to fully cover the valvar and subvalvar obstruction. Following substantial somatic and pulmonary artery growth, complete repair was successfully performed at 5 months and 5.27 kg.

abstract.label: POTENTIAL PITFALLS
abstract.text: Long-sheath positioning across the RVOT may cause hemodynamic instability. Stents should be prepared before sheath advancement, RVOT instrumentation minimized, and operators prepared for expedited deployment. Complete coverage of the dynamic subvalvar obstruction is essential.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: RVOT stenting can provide effective palliation in carefully selected very low birth weight infants, supporting pulmonary artery and somatic growth before definitive repair.

articles.title: Failing Fontan Circulation Bridged to Heart Transplantation With a Surgically Implanted Microaxial Flow Pump

abstract.text: An 18-year-old male patient with Fontan circulation was admitted to our institution with progressive cardiac decompensation. Because of his severely impaired systolic function, he had previously been listed for heart transplantation. Following admission, he rapidly developed cardiogenic shock, necessitating cardiopulmonary resuscitation and intubation. After implantation of a microaxial flow pump through the right subclavian artery, hemodynamics and respiration stabilized quickly; notably, the patient was extubated on the first postoperative day. Sixteen days thereafter, heart transplantation was performed successfully. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Patients with a failing systemic ventricle in Fontan circulation can be successfully bridged to heart transplant by insertion of a microaxial flow pump.

articles.title: Novel Heterozygous NEXN Variant (c.1015del; p.Glu339Lysfs⁎14) Leading to Severe Infantile Dilated Cardiomyopathy Requiring Heart Transplantation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Pathogenic NEXN variants are a rare cause of dilated cardiomyopathy. Heterozygous variants have been associated with a wide phenotypic range, including infantile presentations that typically recover, whereas transplant-requiring infantile disease has been reported only with biallelic genotypes or alongside a second cardiomyopathy gene variant.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: We present a 21-year-old male who underwent orthotopic heart transplantation at 6 months of age for severe infantile dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). Genetic testing identified a novel heterozygous frameshift variant in NEXN (c.1015del; p.Glu339Lysfs⁎14), absent from population databases and classified as pathogenic.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: To our knowledge, this is the first monoallelic NEXN variant reported as the sole candidate genotype in infantile-onset end-stage DCM requiring transplantation. Reported monoallelic disease runs from spontaneous recovery to transplantation, and variant position does not predict severity, so a further factor is likely to be involved.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: Monoallelic NEXN loss of function can cause end-stage infantile DCM. Reported outcomes in children run from spontaneous recovery to transplantation. Retrospective genetic testing of adults transplanted in childhood can establish a molecular diagnosis 2 decades later and redirect screening for their relatives.

articles.title: ECPR-to-Heart Transplant in a Young Woman With PPA2-Associated Metabolic Cardiomyopathy Presenting as Inferolateral STEMI

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: PPA2-related mitochondrial cardiomyopathy is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder associated with rapidly progressive dilated cardiomyopathy, ventricular arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Heightened sensitivity to alcohol has been reported in some affected individuals. Heart transplantation in affected patients is rarely reported.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 21-year-old woman with no prior history presented with chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain, and vomiting after alcohol intake. Electrocardiogram showed inferior and lateral ST-segment elevation. She developed pulseless electrical activity arrest en route to coronary angiography and underwent extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation. Coronary angiography was normal. Echocardiography revealed severe biventricular dysfunction (left ventricular ejection fraction <20%). Despite Impella 5.5 support, no recovery occurred. Whole-genome sequencing identified pathogenic and likely pathogenic PPA2 variants, confirming PPA2-related mitochondrial cardiomyopathy. She underwent successful orthotopic heart transplantation.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case highlights fulminant cardiogenic shock due to PPA2-related cardiomyopathy. Rapid genomic sequencing established the diagnosis when angiography and endomyocardial biopsy were unrevealing, informed prognosis, and enabled genetic counseling and cascade family testing.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: PPA2 cardiomyopathy should be suspected in young patients with arrest, severe ventricular dysfunction, and normal coronaries. Rapid genomic sequencing can be diagnostic and guide management.

articles.title: Papillary Fibroelastoma in Transplant Recipients

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Papillary fibroelastomas (PFEs), benign valvular cardiac tumors, are uncommonly reported in transplant recipients, with management complicated by comorbidities.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: Five patients (ages 27-77 years) underwent heart transplantation, with complicated post-transplant courses, and were maintained chronically on immunosuppression. Surveillance echocardiography identified valvular PFEs, 0.4 to 0.6 cm in size, with timing varying from intraoperative imaging (donor hearts) to 10 years post-transplant.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: The majority of PFEs were clinically silent, small, relatively stable, and, given elevated operative risk, were managed conservatively with continued surveillance. KRAS mutations, reported in ∼33% of PFEs, suggest a neoplastic origin, though the synergistic impact of immunosuppression in PFE growth and proliferation in transplant recipients is unknown. Lack of large databases for PFEs in transplant recipients limits direct comparison with nontransplant patients.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: These cases underscore the value of surveillance imaging and need for balancing surgical risk in management. Prolonged follow-up is needed to clarify natural history and optimal management.

articles.title: Pushing the boundaries in extending cardiac graft preservation: Hypothermic, oxygenated perfusion (HOPE) versus enhanced normothermic perfusion in a porcine model of donation after circulatory death (DCD)
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Excellent outcomes have been reported for heart transplantation with donation after circulatory death (DCD) using graft preservation/evaluation protocols with normothermic ex situ heart perfusion (ESHP); however, little information is available for hypothermic oxygenated perfusion (HOPE). We investigated extending heart preservation with HOPE versus normothermic perfusion (NP) enhanced with plasma exchange using a porcine DCD model.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Healthy male adult pigs underwent simulated DCD with 15 minutes of warm ischemia. Two ESHP groups were included: enhanced NP (continued as long as ventricular contraction/coronary perfusion was maintained) versus HOPE (20 hours pre-defined duration). Cardiac recovery was evaluated in all hearts under normothermic conditions with ex situ left-ventricular loading.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: ESHP was significantly longer in HOPE versus NP hearts (23.5 versus 10.5 hours, p<0.05), while ventricular, vascular and metabolic recovery remained similar. Markers of oxidative stress and myocardial cell death, as well as cytokine release, were significantly reduced with HOPE compared to NP, but increased upon rewarming to levels similar to NP hearts.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Both enhanced NP and HOPE enable extended ESHP of DCD hearts. Although HOPE preservation provides several benefits, such as ESHP times beyond 20 hours and cardioprotection by lowering oxidative stress and inflammation, the transition from HOPE to normothermic conditions poses a risk of rewarming-related damage, and graft evaluation methods during HOPE remain to be developed. Further research towards the optimization of HOPE for DCD hearts is required.

articles.conclusion: Both enhanced NP and HOPE enable extended ESHP of DCD hearts. Although HOPE preservation provides several benefits, such as ESHP times beyond 20 hours and cardioprotection by lowering oxidative stress and inflammation, the transition from HOPE to normothermic conditions poses a risk of rewarming-related damage, and graft evaluation methods during HOPE remain to be developed. Further research towards the optimization of HOPE for DCD hearts is required.

articles.title: Assessment of Medical Urgency for Heart Transplant in Patients With Cardiac Amyloidosis and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Using a Continuous Risk Score

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The current 6-status US heart allocation system uses a treatment-based framework for heart transplantation listing, with status 1 representing the highest urgency. However, this system may inadequately risk-stratify patients with restrictive cardiomyopathy, specifically cardiac amyloidosis (CA) and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), for whom many high-intensity medical and device-based therapies are less effective.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We identified all adult heart transplantation candidates listed between 2019 and 2024 using the Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients. We determined the medical urgency of candidates with CA and HCM using the validated 50-point US-Candidate Risk Score, which incorporates laboratory data and use of mechanical circulatory support.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The study cohort included 26 545 candidates (median age, 56 years; 74% male), of whom 534 were diagnosed with CA (2.0%) and 860 with HCM (3.2%). Overall, patients with CA had significantly higher overall median UC-CRS scores compared with those with HCM and other diagnoses (36, 26, 30; P<0.01), and across statuses 1 to 4. A higher proportion of patients with CA were categorized as high risk (CRS >40) compared with other diagnoses (33% versus 27%; P<0.01), while patients with HCM had the lowest proportion of high-risk scores (22%). Status 2 was the most common status at transplant across all groups, with exceptions at status 2 most frequently used among patients with CA and HCM compared with all others (58%, 70%, 46%; P<0.01).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Patients with CA have higher medical acuity by US-Candidate Risk Score than is reflected in the current 6-status system. Both CA and HCM rely heavily on exceptions to achieve transplantation, highlighting the need for a continuous risk-based allocation model.

articles.conclusion: Patients with CA have higher medical acuity by US-Candidate Risk Score than is reflected in the current 6-status system. Both CA and HCM rely heavily on exceptions to achieve transplantation, highlighting the need for a continuous risk-based allocation model.

articles.title: Trajectory of Pleural effusion and clinical outcomes in acute Heart Failure (TOP-HF): a prospective observational study

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: Pleural effusion (PE) is a common finding in acute heart failure (AHF). However, its trajectory and its prognostic implications have been poorly characterized. We aimed to evaluate the in-hospital and early post-discharge trajectory of PE and its association with clinical outcomes and health-related quality of life.

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: This prospective single-centre study included 100 patients hospitalized with AHF and PE at admission. Pleural effusion severity was serially assessed by thoracic ultrasound at admission, discharge, and 30, 90, and 180 days after discharge. The primary endpoint was the 180-day composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure (WHF). Associations with PE trajectory were assessed using multivariable Cox regression. Health-related quality of life was evaluated with the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire. Median age was 88 years (interquartile range 83-92), 70% were women, and 80% had preserved ejection fraction. Pleural effusion improved during hospitalization in 59%; complete resolution occurred in 20% at discharge and 71.8% at 180 days. After adjustment, PE trajectory was not significantly associated with the composite endpoint [hazard ratio (HR) 1.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.69-2.45; P = 0.417], death (HR 2.34, 95% CI 0.84-6.47; P = 0.103), or WHF (HR 1.20, 95% CI 0.61-2.35; P = 0.598). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire trajectories did not differ significantly by PE trajectory.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Pleural effusion frequently improved during hospitalization and continued to resolve after discharge. Pleural effusion trajectory was not significantly associated with 180-day outcomes in this cohort, whereas residual B-lines at discharge were associated with adverse outcomes.

articles.conclusion: Pleural effusion frequently improved during hospitalization and continued to resolve after discharge. Pleural effusion trajectory was not significantly associated with 180-day outcomes in this cohort, whereas residual B-lines at discharge were associated with adverse outcomes.

articles.title: Right atrial reservoir strain and clinical outcomes after mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The clinical relevance of right atrial (RA) function in patients undergoing mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) remains unclear. We investigated the association between RA reservoir strain (RASr) and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing M-TEER.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We retrospectively assessed RASr using automated two-dimensional strain analytical software in patients undergoing M-TEER. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization after M-TEER.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 298 patients undergoing M-TEER (age 78.1 ± 9.6 years; male 61.1%; and functional mitral regurgitation 64.4%), the median RASr was 19.6% (interquartile range: 10.3-32.5%). Atrial fibrillation, larger RA area, lower left atrial reservoir strain, and lower tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion or right ventricular fractional area change were correlated to lower RASr. Lower RASr was associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome, independently of clinical and echocardiographic characteristics and procedural results (adjusted hazard ratio: 0.96 per 1% increase in RASr, 95% confidence interval: 0.92-0.99, p=0.031). Our maximally selected log-rank statistics showed that the optimal cut-off value of RASr to discriminate the primary outcome was 24%. Incorporating RASr into conventional clinical and echocardiographic parameters improved model fit, with a modest improvement in discrimination for clinical outcome after M-TEER.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Reduced RASr is associated with adverse clinical outcomes after M-TEER. Our findings highlight the potential importance of RASr as a component of right-sided cardiac function. The assessment of RASr may improve risk stratification in patients undergoing M-TEER.

articles.conclusion: Reduced RASr is associated with adverse clinical outcomes after M-TEER. Our findings highlight the potential importance of RASr as a component of right-sided cardiac function. The assessment of RASr may improve risk stratification in patients undergoing M-TEER.

articles.title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement Versus Medical Therapy for Severe Secondary Tricuspid Regurgitation: The TRIPLACE Registry

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) carries a poor prognosis, yet comparative real-world data on transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) versus medical therapy remain limited.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: The aim of this study was to compare clinical outcomes of TTVR versus medical therapy in patients with secondary TR.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This observational study included the TRIPLACE registry (NCT06033274; TTVR cohort, N = 395, 24 centers, 2017-2025) and the Bronx-Valve Registry (NCT05453526; medical therapy cohort, N = 784, single center, 2017-2019). A 30-covariate propensity score was used for overlap weighting, targeting the average treatment effect in the overlap population (ATO). The primary endpoint was the 2-year composite of all-cause mortality or heart failure (HF) hospitalization.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: TTVR achieved ≤ mild TR in 93.7% and ≤ moderate TR in 98.7%. In-hospital mortality was 0.8%. The most common 30-day adverse events were new permanent pacemaker implantation (14.8%) and severe bleeding (6.5%). Median follow-up was 363 days (Q1-Q3: 63-1,151 days). After ATO weighting, all covariates included in the propensity score model achieved exact mean balance (maximum standardized mean difference: 0.000). TTVR was associated with a lower 2-year primary endpoint (ATO-HR: 0.60 [95% CI: 0.40-0.89]; P = 0.012) and lower all-cause mortality (ATO-HR: 0.61 [95% CI: 0.38-0.99]; P = 0.044), whereas HF hospitalization did not differ significantly between groups (ATO-cause-specific HR: 0.69 [95% CI: 0.39-1.24]; P = 0.215).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In this observational comparison, TTVR was associated with a lower 2-year risk of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization compared with medical therapy in patients with secondary TR. These findings should be interpreted in the context of procedure-related risks and the nonrandomized study design.

abstract.label: REGISTRATION
abstract.text: (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter TRIcuspid Valve RePLACEment [TRIPLACE]; NCT06033274).

articles.conclusion: In this observational comparison, TTVR was associated with a lower 2-year risk of all-cause mortality or HF hospitalization compared with medical therapy in patients with secondary TR. These findings should be interpreted in the context of procedure-related risks and the nonrandomized study design.

articles.title: Simultaneous Mitral and Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiac amyloidosis can be accompanied by combined atrioventricular regurgitation, yet same-session transcatheter treatment of both valves in this setting remains rarely reported.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 78-year-old man with wild-type transthyretin amyloid-associated cardiomyopathy, permanent atrial fibrillation, and progressive heart failure under transthyretin amyloidosis-specific medication presented with severe symptomatic mitral and tricuspid regurgitation. Same-session transcatheter edge-to-edge repair was successfully performed using 1 device at the mitral and 2 devices at the tricuspid valve. Mitral and tricuspid regurgitation were reduced from severe to mild-moderate and from torrential to moderate, with intraprocedural final mean gradients of 3 mm Hg and 1 mm Hg, respectively.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: At 1 year, the patient was in New York Heart Association functional class I and II, and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide had decreased from 2,550 to 726 pg/mL.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: In selected patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis with severe symptomatic bivalvular regurgitation, combined transcatheter edge-to-edge repair at both atrioventricular valves may offer an effective treatment option.

articles.title: Stress-Induced Cardiomyopathy as the Initial Presentation of Sato-Variant Cyclic Vomiting Syndrome in a Child

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The Sato variant of cyclic vomiting syndrome (CVS) is characterized by hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis hyperactivation with episodic catecholamine surges, hypertension, and lethargy. Catecholamine-mediated cardiovascular complications have not been characterized in this population.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 6-year-old girl presented with cardiogenic shock and severe left ventricular systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction 11%). Cardiac biomarkers were markedly elevated. Ventricular function recovered within 2 weeks, and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging showed no late gadolinium enhancement, excluding myocarditis. The presentation was consistent with stress-induced (Takotsubo) cardiomyopathy. She was subsequently diagnosed with the Sato variant of CVS after developing recurrent stereotypical vomiting episodes complicated by hypertensive crises (systolic pressures >200 mm Hg). Management with propranolol prophylaxis and on-demand antihypertensives preserved cardiac function over nearly 2 years of follow-up.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This is the first report of stress cardiomyopathy complicating Sato-variant CVS without an arrhythmogenic substrate, demonstrating that episodic catecholamine surges in this subtype can produce life-threatening cardiac complications in children.

articles.title: Aortic Root Replacement and LVAD in Valvular Heart Disease: Bridge to Recovery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: End-stage valvular heart disease with severe myocardial fibrosis is traditionally managed with heart transplantation.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 31-year-old man with bicuspid aortic valve, severe regurgitation, ejection fraction of 16%, and extensive fibrosis (extracellular volume, 39.1%) underwent a Bio-Bentall procedure with left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation. After 27 months of support with optimized guideline-directed medical therapy, ejection fraction recovered to 66%, permitting minimally invasive device explantation. Paired histopathology demonstrated collagen volume fraction regression from 40.26% to 0.65%.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: This case challenges the dogma that severe fibrosis precludes myocardial recovery. The outcome likely reflects synergistic effects of volume overload correction, sustained mechanical unloading, and aggressive neurohormonal blockade. However, bridge to recovery remains uncommon, requires long-term commitment, and is not reproducible in all comparable patients.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Combined Bio-Bentall and LVAD implantation may achieve bridge to recovery in carefully selected young patients with end-stage valvular disease, but patient selection remains critical and outcomes are not guaranteed.

articles.title: Cath Lab Mortality Evaluation: A Methodical Approach in Accordance With Contemporary Best Practices at the World's Largest PCI Center
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Morbidity and Mortality Conferences (MMCs) are essential for enhancing quality in cardiac catheterization laboratories, yet their translation into actionable improvements is often limited. We share our experience with a system-based quality improvement (QI) initiative at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (NICVD) in Karachi, Pakistan, the world's largest primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) center, aimed at enhancing the quality of cath lab operations and patient care for high-risk South Asian patients with acute coronary syndrome.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: From October 2022 to September 2023, a structured MMC-QI framework was implemented to review all 463 cath lab mortalities (from 9265 primary PCIs and 2769 early invasive PCIs). Weekly multidisciplinary reviews by a cardiologist-led committee evaluated patient characteristics, procedural deficiencies, and system delays using standardized forms. Findings were categorized (e.g., technical errors, system inefficiencies) and informed targeted QI interventions, such as streamlined emergency department (ED) triage and enhanced PCI protocols. Descriptive statistics and subgroup analyses (age, gender) were conducted, with door-to-balloon (DTB) times compared pre- and post-intervention.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 463 mortalities (5.4% rate), 64.1% were male (mean age 61.8 ± 10.9 years), 76% had cardiogenic shock, and 87.5% died within 48 h. Key issues included suboptimal stenting (29%), no-reflow/slow-flow complications (22.5%), and inadequate technical approaches (13.2%). Unexpected mortalities (43%) were more common in females (p = 0.039), with higher diagnostic inadequacies (p < 0.001). QI interventions reduced technical issues (23% to 4.3%), procedural complications (33% to 15%), inadequate stenting (40% to 22%), and ED delays (33% to 18%). Median DTB time improved from 115 to 95 min (p < 0.05).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Our experience with an MMC-QI framework demonstrates significant improvements in procedural quality, system efficiency, and care delivery in a high-volume PCI center. While mortality rates remained stable, this system-based approach offers a scalable model for high-burden settings, with potential for broader application pending further evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes.

articles.conclusion: Our experience with an MMC-QI framework demonstrates significant improvements in procedural quality, system efficiency, and care delivery in a high-volume PCI center. While mortality rates remained stable, this system-based approach offers a scalable model for high-burden settings, with potential for broader application pending further evaluation of long-term clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Vector Flow Mapping Energy Loss and Pump Flow in Left Ventricular Assist Device Patients: A Transesophageal Echocardiography Pilot Study
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support redirects intraventricular flow toward the inflow cannula. We examined whether vector flow mapping-derived energy loss (EL), a measure of viscous dissipation related to spatial velocity gradients, was associated with controller-displayed pump flow. This prospective single-center pilot enrolled 33 patients undergoing LVAD-related surgery with intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography; 31 HeartMate 3 recipients were analyzable. The maximum available peak EL across three views was the primary measure. Log-transformed maximum peak EL was associated with displayed flow after adjustment for pump speed and left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (B = 0.181, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.033-0.330), cannula angle (B = 0.204, 95% CI: 0.052-0.356), or aortic regurgitation grade (B = 0.204, 95% CI: 0.050-0.358). Among 28 complete cases, associations persisted using the mean of three view-specific peaks (B = 0.213-0.245; p = 0.007-0.019). In a 10-case interobserver reanalysis, maximum peak EL had an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.759 (95% CI: 0.294-0.934), with ratio limits of agreement of 0.56-2.41. Cannula angle and aortic regurgitation grade were not associated with EL. These preliminary findings support larger prospective studies but do not establish mechanism, measurement interchangeability, or clinical utility.

articles.title: Renal function and outcomes in pulmonary arterial hypertension: a French Pulmonary Hypertension Registry study
authors: on behalf on the French PH Network

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Renal impairment is frequent in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), yet renal function is not currently accounted for in the European Society of Cardiology (ESC)/European Respiratory Society (ERS) risk stratification tools. We investigated whether renal function provides independent prognostic information in PAH after adjustment for ESC/ERS risk score.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the French Pulmonary Hypertension (PH) Network registry. Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was calculated using the 2021 CKD-EPI equation. Renal dysfunction prevalence (eGFR <60 mL·min-1·1.73 m-2) was assessed in patients with PAH (n=3383). Time-to-event analyses for transplant-free survival were performed using Cox models adjusted for age, sex and ESC/ERS risk scores at baseline and at 3-12 months of follow-up.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Renal dysfunction (eGFR <60 mL·min-1·1.73 m-2) was present in 28% of patients with PAH. Baseline eGFR <45 mL·min-1·1.73 m-2 was independently associated with reduced transplant-free survival in multivariable analysis. At 3-12 months of follow-up, eGFR <60 mL·min-1·1.73 m-2 predicted adverse outcomes in multivariable models (hazard ratio 1.25, 95% confidence interval 1.04-1.50; p=0.018). Among patients with preserved baseline renal function, a relative decline in eGFR of ≥10% was independently associated with a higher risk of death or lung transplantation.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Baseline renal impairment and subsequent deterioration in renal function are independently associated with poorer transplant-free survival in PAH, beyond ESC/ERS risk stratification. These findings support consideration of renal function in prognostic assessment of patients with PAH. Baseline renal impairment and subsequent deterioration in renal function are independently associated with poorer transplant-free survival in PAH, beyond ESC/ERS risk stratification.

articles.conclusion: Baseline renal impairment and subsequent deterioration in renal function are independently associated with poorer transplant-free survival in PAH, beyond ESC/ERS risk stratification. These findings support consideration of renal function in prognostic assessment of patients with PAH. Baseline renal impairment and subsequent deterioration in renal function are independently associated with poorer transplant-free survival in PAH, beyond ESC/ERS risk stratification.

articles.title: Left Atrial Stiffness Index and Prognosis Across Heart Failure Phenotypes in Acute Heart Failure: Insights from the STRATS-AHF Registry

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: The left atrial stiffness index (LASI), calculated as mitral E/e' divided by LA reservoir strain, reflects atrial myopathy and elevated filling pressure but has been studied mainly in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF). We examined whether LASI predicts all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization, and adds to established risk factors, across HF phenotypes in acute heart failure (AHF).

abstract.label: METHODS AND RESULTS
abstract.text: We analyzed 3,133 patients with AHF from the multicenter STRATS-AHF registry, classified by LVEF into HFrEF, HFmrEF, and HFpEF. During a median follow-up of 32.5 months, 616 (19.7%) had HF admissions, and 1,281 (40.9%) died. After adjustment, each doubling of LASI was associated with mortality (HR 1.13, 95% CI 1.08-1.19), as was LASI above the exploratory cutoff of 1.0 (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.46). The association was similar across phenotypes (P for interaction = 0.65) and extended to HF hospitalization and the composite of death or HF hospitalization. LASI added modestly to established predictors; after adjustment for NT-proBNP, its association was not significant in patients with a measured value (HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.97-1.10) but persisted after multiple imputation in the whole cohort (HR 1.10, 95% CI 1.04-1.15).

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: In patients hospitalized for AHF, a higher LASI independently predicted all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization across HF phenotypes. Obtained from the admission echocardiogram, LASI captures an atrial component of risk that LVEF does not reflect, although part of this information overlaps with that of NT-proBNP; whether it can guide management remains to be tested.

articles.conclusion: In patients hospitalized for AHF, a higher LASI independently predicted all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization across HF phenotypes. Obtained from the admission echocardiogram, LASI captures an atrial component of risk that LVEF does not reflect, although part of this information overlaps with that of NT-proBNP; whether it can guide management remains to be tested.

articles.title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Isolated Tricuspid Regurgitation After Extended Follow-Up: The TRI-FR Randomized Clinical Trial

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) improves symptoms and health status at 1 year in patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation, but its association with clinical events during longer follow-up remains uncertain.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This secondary analysis reports extended follow-up of TRI-FR (URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04646811), a prospectively registered, multicenter randomized trial comparing T-TEER plus optimized medical therapy (OMT) with OMT alone in patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation. In total, 300 patients were randomized (152 to T-TEER plus OMT and 148 to OMT alone). Prespecified analyses included time to first heart failure hospitalization (HFH), tricuspid surgery, or cardiovascular death using cause-specific Cox proportional-hazards models and recurrent HFH using the Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying model. A 12-month landmark analysis included patients alive and under follow-up at 12 months.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: During a median follow-up of 30.8 months (75th percentile, 41.0; maximum, 56.4), 101 HFHs (17 fatal), 5 additional cardiovascular deaths, and 11 tricuspid surgeries were recorded. Among 81 patients with a first composite event, T-TEER plus OMT reduced the risk versus OMT alone (hazard ratio, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.36-0.88]; P=0.0109). Cardiovascular death or tricuspid surgery did not differ significantly (hazard ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.33-1.71]; P=0.4911). T-TEER plus OMT reduced recurrent HFH (Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying rate ratio, 0.52 [95% CI, 0.32-0.84]; P=0.0073). In the 12-month landmark cohort (n=276), T-TEER plus OMT was associated with lower risks of a first composite event (hazard ratio, 0.40 [95% CI, 0.23-0.70]; log-rank P=0.0009) and recurrent HFH (Lin-Wei-Yang-Ying rate ratio, 0.44 [95% CI, 0.23-0.83]; P=0.0120). Severe or greater tricuspid regurgitation at the last core laboratory assessment was present in 6.77% with T-TEER plus OMT and 53.5% with OMT alone (P<0.0001).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation, T-TEER plus OMT reduced first composite events and recurrent HFH compared with OMT alone during extended follow-up. These associations persisted among patients alive and under follow-up at the 12-month landmark.
