abstract.text: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04646811.

articles.conclusion: In patients with severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation, T-TEER plus OMT reduced first composite events and recurrent HFH compared with OMT alone during extended follow-up. These associations persisted among patients alive and under follow-up at the 12-month landmark.

articles.title: VAD Wean Recovery Network: Long-Term Outcomes of LVAD Weaning for Myocardial Recovery

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Myocardial recovery facilitated by the combination of a left ventricular assist device (LVAD) and guideline-directed medical therapy can lead to sufficient myocardial improvement. This in turn may allow LVAD weaning in appropriately selected patients with chronic advanced heart failure. However, sufficient data on the long-term outcomes of this therapeutic strategy are lacking, thereby hindering widespread adoption of LVAD weaning. We present the primary results from the VAD Wean Myocardial Recovery International Network examining long-term outcomes after LVAD weaning for myocardial recovery.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We studied 603 patients with chronic advanced heart failure from 60 international centers who underwent LVAD weaning. Preimplantation, LVAD cardiac recovery assessment, and postweaning patient characteristics and outcomes were analyzed. The primary outcome was event-free survival (free of heart transplantation or re-LVAD) in the weaned-for-recovery cohort.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The LVAD-weaned cohort had a mean age of 42±15 years; 33% were female; and 9.4% had ischemic cardiomyopathy. At LVAD implantation, 88% had Intermacs (Interagency Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support) profiles 1 to 3, and 41.6% required temporary mechanical circulatory support. Median LVAD support duration was 440 days (interquartile range, 261-770) before weaning. At the time of weaning, median left ventricular ejection fraction was 50% (interquartile range, 45%-57.5%), and left ventricular internal diastolic diameter was 48 mm (interquartile range, 43-53 mm). One-year survival after weaning was 91%, with 2.3% requiring re-LVAD and 3.7% requiring heart transplantation. In a secondary exploratory matched analysis against LVAD bridge-to-transplantation recipients from the International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation registry, long-term survival was similar between groups.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: This international, multicenter analysis suggests that in patients with chronic advanced heart failure achieving myocardial recovery with LVAD support, device weaning yields excellent long-term outcomes. These findings may help address the underuse of LVADs as a bridge-to-recovery strategy in select patients.

articles.conclusion: This international, multicenter analysis suggests that in patients with chronic advanced heart failure achieving myocardial recovery with LVAD support, device weaning yields excellent long-term outcomes. These findings may help address the underuse of LVADs as a bridge-to-recovery strategy in select patients.

articles.title: Ex Situ Echocardiography During Normothermic Perfusion: Serial Physiologic Full Cardiac-Output Assessments for Transplant Suitability
articles.journal: The Journal of heart and lung transplantation : the official publication of the International Society for Heart Transplantation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Clinical normothermic ex situ donor-heart perfusion (NEHP) uses retrograde aortic infusion which prevents hemodynamic assessment. We sought to optimize and validate guideline-directed ex situ echocardiography (ESE) for assessment of transplant suitability using a novel full-cardiac output (FCO) circuit.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: Following transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), porcine hearts were procured and maintained on NEHP for 24 hours. At hours 1, 12, and 24, maintenance NEHP was transitioned to low-preload working-heart mode (LPWH). Although not physiologic, LPWH ensured optimal coronary perfusion and allowed ESE. Hearts were transitioned to physiologic FCO mode and ESE was repeated. NEHP was returned to maintenance. LPWH-ESE and FCO-ESE parameters were compared to determine their ability to stratify function.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Forty-two echocardiograms (6 TTE, 36 ESE) were performed (n=6; 55±8 kg; female 50%; hearts 311±40gm). When compared to FCO-ESE, LPWH-ESE at hour 1 underestimated function (cardiac output (CO) 0.78±0.38 vs 3.26±1.70L/min, p=0.012; cardiac index (CI) 0.0024±0.0010 vs 0.0102±0.0048L/m/gm, p=0.009; stroke volume (SV) 8.0±3.5 vs 30.0±8.2mL, p=0.001; stroke work (SW) 279±102 vs 1683±1134mL/mmHg, p=0.026) and correlation was poor (R2 0.22-0.36). FCO-ESE successfully stratified function between hours 1 and 12 (LVEF 54.6±13.0 vs 33.6±6.0%, p=0.011; CO 3.26±1.70 vs 1.37±0.86L/min, p=0.003; CI 0.0102±0.0048 vs 0.0053±0.0027L/m/gm, p=0.016; SV 30.0±8.2 vs 15.3±6.6mL, p=0.001; SW 1683±1134 vs 686±472mL/mmHg, p=0.029), hours 12 and 24 (LVEF 33.6±6.0 vs 53.0±8.2%, p=0.036, and hours 1 and 24 (SV 30.0±8.2 vs 23.1±6.6mL, p=0.032). LPWH-ESE could not.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Physiologic FCO guideline-directed ESE should facilitate determination of transplant suitability in currently discarded donor hearts and thereby increase the number available for transplantation.

abstract.label: SOCIAL MEDIA
abstract.text: Guideline-directed Ex Situ Echocardiography during physiologic full cardiac output normothermic ex situ perfusion can reproducibly assess donor heart suitability for transplantation #EchoFirst @ASE360 @DHDrake.

articles.conclusion: Physiologic FCO guideline-directed ESE should facilitate determination of transplant suitability in currently discarded donor hearts and thereby increase the number available for transplantation.

articles.title: Outcomes of Catheter Ablation for Ventricular Arrhythmias Performed With ECMO Support: A 10-Year Institutional Experience

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Patients requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) for cardiogenic shock or hemodynamic instability due to ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) represent an extremely high-risk but understudied population. We aimed to evaluate the intraprocedural stability, predictors of in-hospital mortality, and long-term outcomes in patients undergoing ECMO-supported VA ablation.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: This retrospective cohort study included 57 patients undergoing 64 catheter ablations of VAs with ECMO support (2016-2025). Independent predictors of in-hospital mortality were identified using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: The median age of the patients was 62 years, and 70% had ischemic cardiomyopathy. At ECMO initiation, 40 patients (70%) presented with cardiogenic shock and 43 (75%) with electrical storm. ECMO provided robust stability; minimum mean arterial pressure was similar between ventricular and nonventricular tachycardia (55 versus 60 mm Hg; P=0.124). In-hospital mortality was 42% (24/57 [95% CI, 30%-55%]). Multivariable analysis identified age (odds ratio [OR], 1.18 per year [95% CI, 1.05-1.38]; P=0.004), ischemic cardiomyopathy (OR, 24.3 [95% CI, 2.3-700.57]; P=0.005), chronic kidney disease (OR, 9.76 [95% CI, 1.89-73.26]; P=0.006), and New York Heart Association class III or IV (OR, 12.72 [95% CI, 1.86-158.46]; P=0.008) as mortality predictors, whereas VA elimination was an independent protector against in-hospital death (OR, 0.12 [95% CI, 0.01-0.77]; P=0.025). In patients presenting with electrical storm (n=43), VA elimination (n=33) was associated with significantly lower in-hospital mortality than VA recurrence (n=10; 27% versus 80%; P=0.007). Among survivors (n=33), 3-year survival was 78.0%, with low rates of cardiac death (3%, 1/33) during follow-up (11 [3-38] months).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: ECMO-supported VA ablation is feasible and provides procedural stability. Although survival is limited by baseline reserve, VA elimination is associated with improved in-hospital outcomes, serving as a bridge to recovery or clinical decision.

articles.conclusion: ECMO-supported VA ablation is feasible and provides procedural stability. Although survival is limited by baseline reserve, VA elimination is associated with improved in-hospital outcomes, serving as a bridge to recovery or clinical decision.

articles.title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Edge-To-Edge Repair Versus Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement for Severe Symptomatic Tricuspid Regurgitation

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair (T-TEER) and transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) are both approved for severe symptomatic tricuspid regurgitation (TR) but lack head-to-head comparison.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVES
abstract.text: This study sought to compare 1-year outcomes of T-TEER vs TTVR using causal inference in a harmonized real-world cohort.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: TRIVALVE (International Multisite Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Therapies Registry) (T-TEER, n = 384) and TRIPLACE (Global Multicenter Registry on Transcatheter TRIcuspid Valve RePLACEment) (TTVR, n = 398) registries were harmonized (n = 782). Inverse probability weighted survival time estimated study group average treatment effect (ATE) and treated-study group average treatment effect on the treated (ATET) effects on time to all-cause death, heart failure hospitalization (HFH), tricuspid valve (TV) reintervention, bleeding, and their composite major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), balanced for 14 baseline clinical/echocardiographic covariates, were undertaken.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Median follow-up by reverse Kaplan-Meier estimates was 276 days (IQR: 58-365). TTVR achieved near-complete TR elimination vs persistent mild-moderate residual TR post-T-TEER [median (IQR) grade 0 (0-1) vs 2 (1-2)]. Modeling demonstrated an early all-cause mortality penalty for TTVR (ATE: -81.3 days, P = 0.002; ATET: -79 days, P = 0.003) with a corresponding overall MACE signal (ATE: -70.7 days, P = 0.001; ATET: -69.3 days, P = 0.012).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: Despite more complete TR reduction, orthotopic TTVR may be associated with earlier all-cause mortality and MACE penalty over T-TEER. This hypothesis-generating analysis should spur further research to identify the optimal patient phenotype for T-TEER and TTVR technologies.

articles.conclusion: Despite more complete TR reduction, orthotopic TTVR may be associated with earlier all-cause mortality and MACE penalty over T-TEER. This hypothesis-generating analysis should spur further research to identify the optimal patient phenotype for T-TEER and TTVR technologies.

articles.title: A Contemporary Analysis of Microaxial Pump-Associated Cardiac Perforation Events From the FDA MAUDE Database
articles.journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Percutaneous microaxial pumps are used in cardiogenic shock and high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but left ventricular (LV) perforation is an infrequent but serious complication. In 2023, an FDA advisory warned of increased perforation risk.

abstract.label: AIMS
abstract.text: To describe clinical setting, patterns, high-risk subgroups, and outcomes of LV perforation in real-world reports.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We queried the FDA Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database (2016-2024) for Impella adverse-event reports, screened narratives for perforation terms, and manually adjudicated suspected cases to confirm LV perforation and extract device, clinical setting, presentation, management, and outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Among 24,424 Impella reports, 188 involved LV perforation (0.77%). Impella CP accounted for 52.7% and Impella 5.5 for 41.5% (few with 5.0/2.5; none with RP). Annual LV perforations per 1000 reports declined from 166.7 (2016) to 5.2 (2024). Events occurred most often during cardiac surgery (27.1%), acute coronary syndrome (19.1%), or high-risk PCI (17.0%). Intraprocedural diagnosis occurred in 76.2% and was more common with 5.5 versus CP (83.3% vs. 67.7%). With intraprocedural diagnosis, mortality was 24.6% for 5.5 and 28.4% for CP, versus 66.7% for both when diagnosis was post-procedural. Pericardial effusion (34.9%) and hypotension (28.6%) were common. Repair was attempted at 72.9% and reduced mortality, particularly for CP (19.7% with repair vs. 64.7% without; p < 0.001). Overall mortality was 30.2%, without differences by sex or race.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: LV perforation reported with Impella devices is rare but carries high mortality; earlier recognition and prompt repair are associated with improved survival.

articles.conclusion: LV perforation reported with Impella devices is rare but carries high mortality; earlier recognition and prompt repair are associated with improved survival.

articles.title: Cardiopulmonary exercise testing responses to treatment in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension and cardiopulmonary comorbidities

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Current ESC/ERS guidelines suggest that initial monotherapy should be considered for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) with cardiopulmonary comorbidities. However, data on the cardiopulmonary physiological responses to treatment in this subset of patients remain limited. Our aim was to evaluate the cardiopulmonary exercise and gas exchange response to treatment in patients with PAH and cardiopulmonary comorbidities.

abstract.label: RESEARCH QUESTION
abstract.text: Do patients with PAH and a cardiopulmonary phenotype display a worse exercise capacity and gas exchange response to treatment?

abstract.label: STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS
abstract.text: Incident treatment-naïve patients with idiopathic, heritable, drug/toxins-induced, HIV, and connective tissue disease-associated PAH were analysed at first follow-up. Comorbid patients were defined based on the presence of ≥3 risk factors among obesity (body mass index ≥30 Kg/m2), systemic arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease, smoking history and transfer factor of the lung for carbon monoxide (TLCO) <45% predicted.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: A total of 178 patients were included: 52 with comorbidities and 126 without. Comorbid patients were older, predominantly male, and had a lower baseline exercise capacity, despite comparable hemodynamics. There were no differences in therapy, with approximately one third of patients receiving combination therapy in both groups at the time of reassessment. At follow-up, both groups demonstrated similar adjusted improvements from baseline in peak oxygen uptake, oxygen pulse, ventilatory efficiency and 6-minute walk distance, all known prognostic markers in PAH. However, comorbid patients exhibited a significantly worse gas exchange response to treatment, with an adjusted widening of the peak A-a gradient of +1.23 kPa compared with -0.35 kPa in patients without comorbidities (p=0.003).

abstract.label: INTERPRETATION
abstract.text: PAH patients with and without cardiopulmonary comorbidities achieve similar improvements in exercise capacity after treatment. However, the worse gas exchange response to exercise among comorbid patients warrants caution, careful monitoring and further research to confirm this finding.

articles.conclusion: PAH patients with and without cardiopulmonary comorbidities achieve similar improvements in exercise capacity after treatment. However, the worse gas exchange response to exercise among comorbid patients warrants caution, careful monitoring and further research to confirm this finding.

articles.title: Distinct Treg-Mediated Cardiac Remodeling in HFpEF Mice Treated With Neonatal Mesenchymal Stem Cells and Their Secretome

abstract.text: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction lacks effective disease-modifying therapies. We show that neonatal mesenchymal stem cells and their secretome improve diastolic function by expanding regulatory T cells, reducing inflammation and fibrosis. Our new causal machine learning framework, variable importance prediction for cellular function, identified causal immune pathways driving cardiac functional improvement and revealed regulatory T cells as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Hemodynamic Effects of Three Different Mechanical Circulatory Support Strategies in Isolated Acute Right Heart Failure
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Although acute right ventricular failure (aRVF) is commonly treated with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA ECMO), this approach may increase complications. We compared femoro-femoral VA ECMO, single-lumen cannula femoro-pulmonary artery (V-Pa), and double-lumen cannula right atrium-to-pulmonary artery (RA-Pa) support configurations in a swine model of ischemic aRVF-induced cardiogenic shock. Twenty-six adult German Landrasse swine were randomly assigned to the three study groups. Systemic oxygen delivery was the primary end-point; secondary end-points included hemodynamic parameters and complications. Systemic oxygen delivery remained stable during support without intergroup differences. Mean arterial pressure showed higher values in the V-Pa group compared with RA-Pa at 2 hours (65 ± 10 vs. 48 ± 8 mm Hg; p = 0.010) and 3 hours (62 ± 9 vs. 47 ± 10 mm Hg; p = 0.042). Mean pulmonary artery pressure was higher after V-A ECMO (20 ± 5 mm Hg) initiation compared with V-Pa (11 ± 5 mm Hg, p = 0.013) or RA-Pa (11 ± 3 mm Hg, p = 0.006) support. During support, the V-A ECMO group exhibited the lowest EtCO2 and highest carotid flow (p = 0.039 and p < 0.001, respectively). Challenges were noted with double-lumen cannulation due to anatomical constraints. Pulmonary artery cannulation-based support was noninferior to V-A ECMO in terms of oxygen delivery, with lower pulmonary pressures and preserved transpulmonary flow. Femoral vein-to-pulmonary artery configuration showed favorable short-term hemodynamics and easier cannulation compared with RA-Pa.

articles.title: Limited Discrimination of Risk Scores for Right Ventricular Failure After Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation
articles.journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)

abstract.text: Right ventricular failure (RVF) remains a major complication after left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation and is associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Multiple preoperative risk scores and hemodynamic parameters have been proposed to predict RVF; however, their generalizability remains uncertain. We performed a retrospective single-center study of 331 patients undergoing centrifugal-flow LVAD implantation between 2011 and 2025, excluding axial-flow devices. Right ventricular failure, defined by Interagency Registry for Mechanically Assisted Circulatory Support (INTERMACS) criteria, occurred in 105 patients (31.7%). We evaluated established hemodynamic parameters and published risk scores using logistic regression, standalone receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration assessment, and sensitivity analyses. Although several risk scores, including European Registry for Patients with Mechanical Circulatory Support (EUROMACS), Utah, and STOP-RVF, were associated with RVF, their discriminative performance was modest, with area under the curve values around 0.70. Discrimination remained modest in the HeartMate 3 subgroup and when postoperative right-sided mechanical circulatory support requirement was used as a more objective endpoint. Calibration analyses showed that published risk strata did not consistently reproduce original absolute event rates, and the incremental improvement beyond preoperative models for predicting a dynamic, institution-dependent complication. Center-specific risk awareness and proactive perioperative management strategies may better mitigate RVF risk.

articles.title: Mechanical Tricuspid Valve Thrombosis Treated With Ultrasound-Assisted Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Mechanical tricuspid valves are remarkably susceptible to acute mechanical valve thrombosis (MVT). Current guidelines suggest reoperation or systemic thrombolysis for left-sided MVT. These treatments carry substantial operative and bleeding risks, limiting their application. A better nonsurgical treatment for MVT is needed.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: Six patients with suspected acute tricuspid MVT were treated with ultrasound-assisted catheter-directed thrombolysis (USCDT). Improvement in symptoms, leaflet mobility, and tricuspid regurgitation severity occurred in 5 of 6 cases with no observed complications. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES?: Tricuspid MVT is not addressed in current guidelines because of a paucity of available data.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: USCDT represents a novel treatment alternative for tricuspid MVT. Direct contact between the USCDT catheter and the mechanical valve may enhance alteplase activity and thrombus dispersion.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: USCDT may represent an alternative to contemporary treatments for tricuspid MVT and warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Replacement in a 9-Year-Old Boy Using a 48-mm Self-Expanding Transcatheter Bioprosthesis

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: A 9-year-old boy with hypoplastic left ventricle developed severe tricuspid regurgitation and symptomatic right heart failure after complex biventricular conversion. Given 4 prior sternotomies, transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) was considered. Computed tomography demonstrated severe septal leaflet tethering and posterior leaflet-papillary muscle continuity, limiting leaflet-dependent devices. Our objective was deployment of a self-expanding Intrepid valve that anchors without leaflet capture.

abstract.label: KEY STEPS
abstract.text: A 48-mm Intrepid valve was implanted transfemorally through a 35-F sheath under transesophageal echocardiographic and fluoroscopic guidance, achieving stable positioning and excellent tricuspid regurgitation reduction.

abstract.label: POTENTIAL PITFALLS
abstract.text: Abnormal anatomy may compromise leaflet-dependent stability. Large-bore venous access requires careful planning in pediatric patients, and post-TTVR anticoagulation is necessary to reduce prosthetic valve thrombosis risk.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGES
abstract.text: In selected pediatric patients at high surgical risk, TTVR may provide an effective alternative therapy. When leaflet anatomy is unfavorable, devices that anchor independently of leaflet capture may offer a practical solution.

articles.title: Sotatercept in pulmonary arterial hypertension with suspected venous involvement: a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: The use of sotatercept in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and suspected pulmonary venous involvement is limited.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 43-year-old man with PAH, marked hypoxaemia, severely reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide, and a sister with autopsy-proven occlusive pulmonary venous disease deteriorated despite three-drug combination therapy. Whole-genome sequencing identified no pathogenic EIF2AK4 variants, and no pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were found in 18 other PAH-associated genes, including BMPR2. After 3 months of sotatercept treatment, clinical (functional class III to II), haemodynamic (pulmonary vascular resistance 11.6 to 8.1 Wood units), and right ventricular functional improvement (ejection fraction 25.0% to 37.6% on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging) were observed without pulmonary oedema or worsening hypoxaemia.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Sotatercept may have potential clinical relevance and a tolerable safety profile in patients with PAH and suspected pulmonary venous involvement. Careful monitoring of oxygenation and pulmonary oedema remains essential, and further evidence is needed to define the role of this treatment in this challenging population.

articles.title: Dual obstructive physiology in Takotsubo cardiomyopathy: cardiac tamponade exacerbating systolic anterior motion-mediated left ventricular outflow tract obstruction-a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy may be complicated by dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) due to basal hyperkinesis in response to apical akinesis. In turn, this can lead to complications such as mitral regurgitation (MR) and systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve, resulting in hypotension and potentially cardiogenic shock.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 72-year-old woman presented with chest pain and ST elevation. Coronary angiography was normal, with left ventriculography and subsequent transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) confirming a diagnosis of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. She developed refractory cardiogenic shock from severe LVOTO with SAM and MR, unresponsive to traditional therapies such as intravenous fluids, beta-blockade, and vasopressors. Serial TTE demonstrated progression of a small pericardial effusion with evolving tamponade physiology. Emergent pericardiocentesis resulted in immediate improvement of the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) gradient, elimination of valvular pathologies, and rapid haemodynamic recovery.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: LVOT obstruction due to hyperdynamic basal contraction and mitral SAM is a known cause of cardiogenic shock, particularly in cardiomyopathies where apical ballooning is a feature. Progressive pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade may critically exacerbate LVOTO, MR, and mitral SAM through preload reduction and render standard LVOT-directed therapy ineffective. As early recognition and treatment of tamponade physiology can be lifesaving, failure to respond to LVOT-directed therapy should warrant urgent repeat echocardiography.

articles.title: Diagnostic yield of genetic testing in heart transplant recipients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: A single-center cohort study

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Cardiomyopathy genetic testing is recommended for patients with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) but is inconsistently applied once a patient has reached end-stage disease and undergone heart transplantation. Whether a transplant program can systematically test its existing NICM cohort and what completion rate is achievable when testing is operationalized in the clinic rather than offered ad hoc is not well characterized.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We studied all 73 adults followed in the Southern Alberta Transplant Program after transplantation for NICM: dilated (DCM), non-dilated left ventricular (NDLVC), restrictive, or hypertrophic (HCM). Cardiomyopathy genetic testing was offered as a program-wide initiative and performed in adulthood using clinically validated multigene panels. Variants were classified by ACMG/AMP criteria; pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants interpreted as explanatory for the recipient's cardiomyopathy were counted as diagnostic. Single heterozygous P/LP variants in autosomal recessive genes were interpreted as carrier findings and not counted toward yield. Yields are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs); the childhood- versus adult-transplant comparison was tested with Fisher's exact test.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 71 eligible patients, 27 (38.0%) had a genetic-testing result before the 12-month operational window; of the 44 offered testing during the window, 37 completed it (84.1%), raising cohort testing coverage to 90.1% (64/71). A diagnostic pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) variant was identified in 28 of 64 tested patients (43.8%; 95% CI 32.3%-55.9%); a sensitivity analysis restricted to the 36 patients tested with the comprehensive Invitae 121-gene panel yielded an indistinguishable 38.9% (14/36; 95% CI 24.8%-55.1%), with no evidence that variation in panel breadth materially biased the overall estimate. Two additional patients carried a single heterozygous P/LP variant in an autosomal recessive gene (carrier findings, not counted). Yield was higher in patients transplanted in childhood (10/14, 71.4%) than in adulthood (18/50, 36.0%; Fisher's exact P = 0.031). TTN was the most frequent gene (7 P/LP), followed by LMNA, PKP2, and MYH7 (3 each).

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: A 12-month program-wide initiative raised cardiomyopathy genetic testing coverage in an existing NICM heart transplant cohort from 38% to 90% by embedding testing in routine transplant clinic visits. The diagnostic yield among tested patients (43.8%) was consistent with published estimates and similar when restricted to the most comprehensive panel, with markedly higher yield in patients transplanted in childhood. These findings provide a reproducible operational template for transplant programs seeking to close the implementation gap in cardiomyopathy genetic evaluation and to enable cascade testing of at-risk relatives.

articles.conclusion: A 12-month program-wide initiative raised cardiomyopathy genetic testing coverage in an existing NICM heart transplant cohort from 38% to 90% by embedding testing in routine transplant clinic visits. The diagnostic yield among tested patients (43.8%) was consistent with published estimates and similar when restricted to the most comprehensive panel, with markedly higher yield in patients transplanted in childhood. These findings provide a reproducible operational template for transplant programs seeking to close the implementation gap in cardiomyopathy genetic evaluation and to enable cascade testing of at-risk relatives.

articles.title: Complex management of ATTRv amyloidosis (Glu89Gln) amid haemodynamic instability and heart failure: a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: ATTRv with the NM_000371.4:c.325G>C, p.Glu109Gln (legacy p.Glu89Gln) mutation, reported in endemic clusters in southern Italy and Bulgaria, is characterized by an aggressive mixed cardio-neurological phenotype. The disease typically manifests around the age of 50. The burden of altered haemodynamics and orthostatic intolerance superimposed on the restrictive cardiomyopathy makes advanced heart failure (HF) management a significant clinical challenge.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: We present the case of a 59-year-old male with ATTRv amyloidosis carrying the Glu89Gln mutation, alongside Type 2 diabetes and macroalbuminuric nephropathy. Despite a genetic diagnosis in 2006 following carpal tunnel syndrome and mild orthostatic hypotension, cardiac involvement was only formally recognized in 2022. Following a period of stability on tafamidis 61 mg/day, he developed weight gain, refractory right-sided acute HF, and cardio-renal syndrome in 2026. Severe diuretic resistance and hypotension (<95 mmHg) occurred. A large-volume paracentesis (>10 l) was performed and plausibly contributed to the marked improvement in renal function and the restoration of diuretic responsiveness. As a net result of the overall strategy, a 32-kg net weight reduction was achieved over 13 days, leading to discharge in NYHA class II and an improvement in the Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT) distance.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Managing congestion in patients with restrictive physiology and susceptibility to hypotension requires multidisciplinary approaches, including unconventional ones, such as evacuative paracentesis. Furthermore, adapting disease-modifying therapies requires careful shared decision-making, balancing the potential benefits of gene silencers with real-world patient preferences and clinical stability.

articles.title: Fulminant myocarditis across the aetiological spectrum in the era of mechanical circulatory support: a case series

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Fulminant myocarditis is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by acute haemodynamic compromise, malignant arrhythmias, and rapid progression to cardiogenic shock. Although the clinical presentation is often uniform, the underlying aetiology is heterogeneous and carries important implications for diagnosis, therapeutic strategy, and prognosis.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: We report four patients presenting within months of each other with fulminant myocarditis of distinct aetiologies: eosinophilic myocarditis associated with amoxicillin-clavulanate in a 71-year-old male; a suspected lymphocytic myocarditis in a 25-year-old male with a posthumously identified pathogenic FLNC (Filamin C) variant; lymphocytic myocarditis with extensive replacement fibrosis in a 68-year-old male; and virus-negative lymphocytic myocarditis in a 61-year-old female. All four required mechanical circulatory support. Outcomes ranged from death in two patients to survival with durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support in one and complete functional recovery after transient support in another.

abstract.label: CONCLUSION
abstract.text: Endomyocardial biopsy was pivotal in establishing the underlying diagnosis and guiding management. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) showed supporting findings but was most valuable raising the possibility of alternative diagnosis such as arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. These cases illustrate that fulminant myocarditis represents a haemodynamic phenotype rather than a final diagnosis. Systematic histological, virological, and-where clinically indicated-genetic evaluation is essential, as aetiology informs management but does not reliably predict outcome in mechanical circulatory support (MCS)-dependent presentations.

articles.title: National Dissemination of a Decision Aid for Patients Considering a Left Ventricular Assist Device

abstract.label: IMPORTANCE
abstract.text: For patients with end-stage heart failure considering a left ventricular assist device (LVAD), shared decision-making is encouraged by guidelines and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). Patients, caregivers, and clinicians have reported suboptimal guidance and support for LVAD decision-making, including a lack of unbiased educational materials.

abstract.label: OBJECTIVE
abstract.text: To disseminate a tested patient decision aid (PDA) as standard practice in all LVAD programs across the US.

abstract.label: DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS
abstract.text: From 2018 to 2023, this I-DECIDE-LVAD initiative built a network of contacts across US CMS-certified LVAD programs to promote adoption and support implementation of the PDA to clinicians at LVAD programs and their patients considering an LVAD. Responses to all implementation assessments were collected and data analysis was conducted in October 2022 and mostly completed by January 2024.

abstract.label: INTERVENTIONS
abstract.text: An LVAD PDA, consisting of a pamphlet and video, that was previously shown to improve decision quality.

abstract.label: MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES
abstract.text: This mixed-methods evaluation was guided by the RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance) framework, where an implementation assessment was collected among clinicians every 4 to 6 months; a subset of clinicians was interviewed and a subset of patients surveyed for a more comprehensive understanding of outcomes.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Of 175 certified LVAD programs, all were successfully contacted and 169 (96.6%) adopted the PDAs. Over 4 years of follow-up, 156 programs responded to the implementation assessments; 123 (70.3%) reported active use, including 80 (45.7%) using the PDA as standard of care and 23 (13.1%) using it frequently. Overall, 7132 patients received the PDA, representing 83.2% of eligible patients at participating programs. Of the 205 patients who completed a survey across 16 programs (mean [SD] age, 62 [13] years; 50 females [24.4%]), 127 (62.0%) reported receiving the pamphlet and 79 (38.5%) received the video. Facilitators to PDA implementation included flexibility in how it could be used, positive opinions of and experiences with the PDA, and ease of integration within existing program structure. Common barriers included limited implementation capacity or preference for existing materials.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE
abstract.text: This nationwide quality improvement study of LVAD medical decision-making found that 70.3% of all LVAD programs in the US reported using a proven effective PDA with their patients. This initiative suggests that this is one of the broadest and most successful implementation efforts of a PDA.

articles.title: Normothermic regional perfusion versus direct procurement with machine perfusion in donation after circulatory death heart transplantation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of early and mid-term outcomes

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Donation after circulatory death (DCD) is now a major source of cardiac allografts, yet the two dominant recovery strategies, thoraco-abdominal normothermic regional perfusion (NRP) and direct procurement with ex-situ machine perfusion (DP-MP), have never been compared in a dedicated meta-analysis of clinically meaningful endpoints.

abstract.label: METHODS
abstract.text: We systematically searched five databases and grey literature for studies comparing NRP with DP-MP in adult DCD heart transplantation. Random-effects models generated pooled risk ratios (RR), with Hartung-Knapp sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was severe primary graft dysfunction (PGD); secondary outcomes were survival, treated acute cellular rejection (ACR) and cost. Risk of bias and certainty were assessed with ROBINS-I and GRADE.

abstract.label: RESULTS
abstract.text: Eight studies were included, three pooled for PGD. NRP was associated with less severe PGD (RR 0.38, 95% CI 0.25-0.60; n = 728; Hartung-Knapp 0.25-0.59) and less treated ACR at one year (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.35-0.76). Overlapping registry cohorts were de-duplicated; 30-day survival did not differ (RR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00-1.04; P = 0.073), and a borderline one-year difference (RR 1.04, 95% CI 1.00-1.08) was not robust to registry substitution, indicating equivalent survival. Cost favoured NRP; certainty was moderate.

abstract.label: CONCLUSIONS
abstract.text: In adult DCD heart transplantation, thoraco-abdominal NRP was associated with lower rates of severe PGD and treated acute cellular rejection, at equivalent survival and lower cost. As the data are observational, these estimates remain imprecise and subject to residual confounding. NRP is reasonable where feasible, and adequately powered trials with standardised adjudication of graft dysfunction are needed.

articles.title: Catastrophic in-stent thrombosis with antiphospholipid syndrome: a case report

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: In-stent thrombosis despite morphologically optimal stents remains a diagnostic challenge. Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a rare cause that drives thrombosis via tissue factor-mediated coagulation-a pathway not addressed by dual antiplatelet therapy.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 51-year-old male with cardiovascular risk factors underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention for anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Ten days later, he developed refractory ventricular fibrillation requiring extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation with veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and intra-aortic balloon pump support. Emergency angiography confirmed complete in-stent thrombosis; intravascular ultrasound excluded a mechanical cause. The intensive care course revealed a triad of red flags: unexplained in-stent thrombosis, recurrent extracorporeal circuit clotting despite stepwise heparin escalation, and arterial and venous thrombosis on full anticoagulation. This prompted antiphospholipid antibody testing, which showed persistent moderate-to-high titre anti-cardiolipin IgM-a profile within the 'controversial' zone of the 2023 ACR/EULAR classification criteria. The patient was managed as APS with intensified triple therapy, later transitioning from heparin to a vitamin K antagonist, and was discharged on Day 27 with no events at 3-month follow-up.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Antiphospholipid syndrome should be considered in unexplained in-stent thrombosis even when laboratory criteria are not strictly met. The triad of unexplained in-stent thrombosis, anticoagulation refractory circuit clotting, and incident venous thrombosis is a clinically actionable pattern warranting empiric APS-directed management.

articles.title: Atrial Septal Defect Repair After Reverse Potts Shunt for Severe Pulmonary Hypertension

abstract.label: BACKGROUND
abstract.text: Atrial septal defect (ASD) closure in the presence of a functioning reverse Potts shunt (rPS) for pulmonary hypertension (PH) may reduce global hypoxemia without sacrificing right ventricular pressure unloading. However, intracardiac operation after rPS has not previously been reported to guide operative decision-making in this scenario.

abstract.label: CASE SUMMARY
abstract.text: A 13-year-old girl with a history of rPS for PH presented for ASD closure because of hypoxia and exercise intolerance. To safely close the ASD on cardiopulmonary bypass, the rPS was occluded with a catheter-based balloon.

abstract.label: DISCUSSION
abstract.text: Coexisting ASD and rPS in a patient with severe PH presents a complex hemodynamic scenario. Furthermore, intracardiac operation in the setting of patent rPS and PH presents certain technical challenges. Multidisciplinary care is necessary for safe and effective management of coexisting ASD and rPS.

abstract.label: TAKE-HOME MESSAGE
abstract.text: Balloon occlusion of reverse Potts shunt can be safely performed in select patients to expand feasibility for repair of intracardiac defects in PH.
